issues.description: The problem statement (and the template Main) refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to handle deliveries, but the solution implements this functionality as a differently named static method receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This name mismatch between the specified API (acceptSupplyDelivery) and the solution (receiveDelivery) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about the required method name and will break any code (e.g., Main) that calls acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery with the same signature (public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)), or alternatively update the problem statement and template code to use receiveDelivery consistently. Ensure the method remains static and has the parameters (String, int, int) as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the example Main) refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) to register incoming stock deliveries, but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) in SealSaloon. This is the same conceptual operation with two different identifiers, which breaks the direct mapping from the exercise specification and example usage to the implemented API and may confuse students about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the delivery-accepting method across all artifacts. Either rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity), or update the problem statement and example Main to call receiveDelivery. Preferably align the solution with the problem statement and example by implementing acceptSupplyDelivery.
